messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: EU data residency & export-control follow-up — post-demo Q&A

Hi Lucie / EuroFinTech team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really helpful to walk through your residency and compliance checklist. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same view: 

Summary of asks from your side
- SOC 2 Type II status and any redacted evidence we can share for procurement review.
- Confirmation of EU-region availability and cross-border transfer policy (we discussed EU-only processing and encrypted key control).
- Vendor security questionnaire completion and answers re: OFAC/ITAR controls.
- HIPAA / health-data handling — whether Redwood's offering can meet a BAA for your use-case.

What I can confirm right now (high level)
- EU hosting: Redwood offers an EU-hosted region (eu-west-1) for the hosted API and can provision Dedicated pools in EU regions. Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments are available for regulated workloads.
- Data residency & cross-border transfers: we support strict routing to EU-hosted capacity and customer-managed key options; cross-border exports are subject to policy and may require a documented data-flow agreement.
- SOC 2: Redwood is in SOC 2 Type II readiness — we can provide a redacted readiness summary and our compliance roadmap. Full Type II report expected in early 2027 (I'll confirm timeline below).
- OFAC/ITAR: we perform screening and have an escalation process; ITAR-controlled data is a special case and typically requires private/on-prem deployments and an export-control review.
- HIPAA: we can support HIPAA-covered workloads via Private deployments with a BAA; hosted (multi-tenant) options require review.

Requested next steps
1) Lucie — can you send the vendor questionnaire (PDF) you mentioned? I will coordinate answers and get the right tech and compliance artifacts attached.
2) Karthik / Marissa — I need SOC 2 readiness summary (redacted), a short note on live EU region names and whether Dedicated provisioning can be completed within 2 weeks, and an explicit ITAR/OFAC stance we can include in the questionnaire.
3) I'll follow up with a draft questionnaire response and a one-pager on data flows for your legal team.

Attachments: placeholder for SOC2 readiness summary (we'll attach a redacted PDF).

Thanks — talk soon.

— Soojin

Thanks for the clear recap — exactly what we needed. Attaching the vendor security questionnaire (please return with responses where possible). A few clarifications from our side: 
- Procurement will need either a SOC 2 Type II report or a redacted SOC 2 evidence pack to move forward.
- We must confirm EU-only processing for production data; please indicate the exact regions and whether keys/data ever move to non-EU hosts.
- ITAR/OFAC: we handle regulated export controls strictly — please identify whether Redwood has any customers or infra in jurisdictions that would trigger export review, and provide any existing export-control policies.
- HIPAA: indicate whether Redwood will sign a BAA for Private deployments; we will not accept multi-tenant hosted without a BAA for sensitive health data.

We expect a completed questionnaire within 7 business days to progress to legal review.

Hey team — notes below (copyable text for the questionnaire).

1) EU regions & provisioning - Hosted (multi-tenant) EU region: eu-west-1 (live) — used for lower-compliance workloads.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): can be provisioned in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1; typical lead time 7–14 business days depending on capacity and sizing.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): available for air-gapped or regulated customers; on-prem deployments follow our private installer checklist.

2) Data residency / cross-border transfer
- By default, requests targeted at EU region are served within the EU host boundary and do not leave the region for inference.
- Customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted customers may use Redwood-managed keys but we offer region-restricted key storage on request.
- Cross-border transfer: any data export outside EU requires documented approval and a data-flow agreement; for legal teams we provide a Data Flow One-Pager.

3) SOC 2 & evidence
- SOC 2 Type II: Redwood is currently in the Type II readiness phase; estimated report completion Q1 2027 (target date 2027-02-15).
- Action: I uploaded a redacted SOC2 readiness summary and control-mapping to our drive: https://drive.redwood.internal/teams/compliance/soc2/eft-redacted-summary-2026-11-14.pdf

4) OFAC / ITAR stance
- OFAC: We screen customers and accounts for sanctions as part of onboarding; any flagged accounts require export-control approval and potential denied service.
- ITAR: Redwood does not permit ITAR-controlled data on our standard hosted multi-tenant service. ITAR workloads may be supported only on Private (on-prem) deployments after an export-control review and contractual controls.

5) HIPAA / BAA
- Redwood can sign a BAA for Private deployments and will implement required administrative, technical, and physical controls. Multi-tenant hosted environments require an additional legal review and are not standard for high-risk PHI.

Suggested copy for questionnaire (paste as needed):
"Redwood Inference offers EU-hosted and Dedicated capacity with region-restricted processing. Customer-managed KMS/HSM is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. SOC 2 Type II report is expected Q1 2027; we can provide a redacted readiness summary for procurement review. Export-controlled data (ITAR) is not supported on our hosted platform; Private/on-prem deployments are available pending export-control review. OFAC screening is applied during onboarding. For HIPAA-covered workloads, we offer a BAA for Private deployments."

If you want, I can pre-fill the questionnaire with the above and share a draft.

— Karthik
